edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource.

basis.zh: 汉代乐府民歌，作者不详。

note.en: An anonymous Han dynasty yuefu, a song of the kind collected by the imperial Music Bureau. Its last couplet became a proverb that Chinese schoolchildren still copy into their notebooks. It sits on this shelf as the plainest statement of the library's other half: the rivers run one way, so carry something on while you can.
note.zh: 汉乐府民歌，作者不详。末两句成了格言，至今还被小学生抄在本子上。放在这里，是因为它最直白地说出了这座图书馆的另一半：百川东流不回头，所以趁还来得及，把一些东西传下去。

excerpt.orig: 百川東到海，何時復西歸？
excerpt.en: A hundred rivers flow east to the sea: / when will any of them come back west?
excerpt.zh: 百川东到海，何时复西归？
